clue.text: Poor game worked on

indicators.note: worked suggests something kneaded or reshaped, so the letters of game are rearranged

parts.note: on in the sense of about or concerning gives RE

explanation.surface: A sportsman's game has been worked on, yet remains disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' makes MEAG; 'on' means concerning, as in a memo heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something scanty or inadequate in amount or quality.

clue.text: I: setter's I keeps working

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says my

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: in this puzzle I stands for a Greek island, here Kos
working, as a machine is, means on

explanation.surface: A setter declares that his own self keeps on working.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle I stands for a Greek island, both as definition and in the wordplay. 'keeps' puts ON inside KOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme makes I mean a Greek island, and this Cycladic holiday island is one.

clue.text: Stick mark on ballot paper, if nothing turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, slang for nothing at all
voters mark their choice with a cross, X

explanation.surface: A voter is told to make a mark on the ballot if no candidate appeals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives AFFI. Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick something on is to attach or fasten it, as with a stamp or label.

clue.text: Loving son snared by hen, girl I suspect

indicators.note: snared by means caught inside, so the son's letter is trapped within the rest
suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a boy has been trapped by a hen party and a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' makes RELIHING; 'snared by' puts the son's letter inside it. 'I suspect' reads as a comment, but I is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoying something greatly, taking great pleasure in it, is a sense of being fond of it.

clue.text: 15 on 5 scored highly

indicators.note: the answer to 15 across can be read as re-sort, an instruction to rearrange the letters

parts.note: the answer to 5 down is the island Paros

explanation.surface: A holiday spot sitting above an island earned top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across read as re-sort is the anagram signal: ON and PAROS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A part written for the highest voice in a musical score is pitched at the top of the range.

clue.text: Turner's viaduct?

parts.note: a wrench that turns nuts, and a bridge that crosses a gap, are both things that span; the painter Turner is the false lead

explanation.surface: A query about a viaduct painted by JMW Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but it means something that turns, i.e. a tool for nuts; a viaduct is literally something that crosses a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nut-turning tool in British English and anything that bridges a span.

clue.text: I thus blow up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: thus means so
a blow or knock is a rap

explanation.surface: Someone resolves this way to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: I is a Greek island in this puzzle. 'up' reverses SORAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme makes I mean a Greek island, and this Cycladic marble island is one.

clue.text: Puzzling old friend, artist in middle of saucy song

indicators.note: in places the artist's letters inside the other piece
middle of takes the letters of saucy without its first and last

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: An old pal, a painter, sits amid a cheeky ditty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives AUC from saucy; 'in' puts RA into it for ARAUC. The answer is the pseudonym of the late John Graham, a much-loved Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the pen-name of a famous Guardian compiler, a long-time friend to solvers of puzzles.

clue.text: Keep thinking only about entering classes boxer set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
entering signals letters found going into the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boxer joining classes can think of nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'entering' in the definition, but it is the signal for the concealed letters in claSSES BOxer; 'set up' then turns them round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be preoccupied with something, dwelling on it constantly, is to fixate on it.

clue.text: Still a 5th Avenue, perhaps?

parts.note: Fifth Avenue is an example of a thoroughfare in New York

explanation.surface: A question whether Fifth Avenue is still the same.
explanation.walkthrough: NY is New York; a way is a road, and Fifth Avenue is one there.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and nonetheless are both used to mean in spite of that, regardless.

clue.text: I leak info about article

indicators.note: about in the sense of around or astray signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to passing information about a news piece.
explanation.walkthrough: I is a Greek island in this puzzle. 'about' rearranges LEAK INFO into KEFALONI; A ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme makes I mean a Greek island, and this large Ionian island is one.

clue.text: Figurative career choices, I say?

indicators.note: say here means spoken out loud, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: in this puzzle I stands for a Greek island, here Rhodes

explanation.surface: Someone muses on their possible career paths.
explanation.walkthrough: I is a Greek island; Rhodes said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths in life, as in 'the road to success', are metaphorical routes one might take.

clue.text: I recall almost all there eating beef

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the letters are taken in reverse order
eating means taking in, so one piece is swallowed by the other
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: someone all there is of sound mind, sane
beef comes from an ox

explanation.surface: Someone remembers nearly everyone there eating beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims to SAN; 'eating' gives SOXAN; 'recall' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme makes I mean a Greek island, and this largest of the Cyclades is one.

clue.text: Airport fliers caught in snow skid all over the place

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for caught inside the jumbled letters
all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Planes caught in a snowy skid slide all over the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' makes WINDSOKS; 'in' places the cricket abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric cones flown on poles at airfields show wind direction, so they are things that fly there.

clue.text: I pinched rear of cop in a sexy manner

indicators.note: pinched means squeezed, so the island grips a letter inside it

parts.note: in this puzzle I stands for an island, here Sicily

indicators.note: rear of picks the last letter of cop

explanation.surface: A confession of groping a policeman's backside in a racy way.
explanation.walkthrough: I is an island; 'pinched' tucks P inside SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something racy or risqué is called spicy, and this adverb describes acting in that titillating way.

clue.text: Poor substitute shows weakness, missing header

indicators.note: missing header means losing the first letter, the top of a down light

parts.note: a limitation is a weakness or shortcoming

explanation.surface: A weak stand-in reveals its flaws, lacking a header like a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing header' drops the first letter of LIMITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy or fake is an inferior replacement for the genuine article.

clue.text: Holiday homes or possible location of holiday

indicators.note: homes as a verb means houses or gives shelter to, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a holiday is a rest

explanation.surface: A choice between holiday homes or a holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday homes' looks like accommodation, but 'homes' is the verb: REST houses OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside or ski town that attracts vacationers is a place people go for a break.

clue.text: Eastern doubly eclipsed by western brews — something in the tea?

indicators.note: eclipsed by means hidden inside, so the doubled letter sits within the jumbled word
brews means stews or mixes up, signalling the letters are rearranged
doubly means the letter is written twice

explanation.surface: A tea-blender's description of eastern leaves outshone by western brews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brews' makes SWTENER; 'doubly' gives two Es, which 'eclipsed by' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar or a sugar substitute is added to a cuppa to make it less bitter.

clue.text: One left in burn

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the other word

parts.note: to singe is to burn lightly

explanation.surface: The sole survivor left in a stream (a burn is a Scottish brook).
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like the Scottish word for a stream but means singe; 'in' places L within.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary item, a lone unit, is just a single one.

clue.text: English XI go

parts.note: the letter X stays as written and the I is an island, here Crete

explanation.surface: England's cricket team, the eleven, must go.
explanation.walkthrough: XI looks like a team of eleven, but it is X plus I, the island. 'go' in the sense of relieving oneself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is a colloquial euphemism for passing waste from the body, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Young cuckoo eaten by goose, having dropped guts

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, signalling the letters of eaten are jumbled
dropping its guts leaves just the outside letters of goose

explanation.surface: A young cuckoo gets eaten by a goose, which has been gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' rearranges EATEN into TEENA; 'having dropped guts' leaves GE from goose.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone aged thirteen to nineteen, i.e. youthful.

clue.text: Where the I's are found and what I's are

definitions.meaning: the islands of this puzzle lie in the Mediterranean Sea, informally the Med
every I in this puzzle stands for an island, so they are organised around a theme

explanation.surface: A double hint about the islands in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way it is THE MED, the Mediterranean; as one word it describes clues built on a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean holds the Greek islands, and the islands are the puzzle's unifying subject.

clue.text: Officer in Jag involved in a specific race

indicators.note: in places the officer inside the car

parts.note: the E-Type was a classic Jaguar sports car
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer in a Jaguar takes part in a particular race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a motor race but is a biological one; the E-Type was a famous 1960s Jaguar.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use the term for a population of a species adapted to particular local conditions, a kind of subspecies.

clue.text: I must collect new bags

indicators.note: must collect means takes in, so the island gathers a letter inside it

parts.note: in this puzzle I stands for a Greek island, here Chios

explanation.surface: Someone insists on collecting new handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: I is a Greek island; 'must collect' puts N inside CHIOS. Bags is old British slang for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags, meaning baggy trousers, covers casual cotton twill trousers.

clue.text: Pick up hairy thing, suffering

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
a 'tache, short for moustache, is a hairy thing

explanation.surface: Someone picks up something hairy and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like lifting, but it means catching a sound; 'tache is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional anguish or grief, such as after a loss, is a kind of suffering.

clue.text: Not entirely competent, he set cryptic clues?

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words is used, the letters concealed inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A grumble that a setter's clues show some incompetence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across competenT HE SEt. The definition points at the very clues the solver is reading, as in 'these clues'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points at things close at hand, here the puzzle's own clues in front of the solver.

clue.text: Old African leader getting wee cut from circular instrument

indicators.note: cut from means removed out of the following piece

parts.note: a tambourine is a round percussion instrument
wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: An old African statesman loses his wee drum.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Tambo led the ANC in exile during apartheid.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Tambo, president of the African National Congress, was a historic South African figure.

clue.text: I drink ale, primarily

parts.note: malt, short for malt whisky, is a drink

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the first letter of ale is used

explanation.surface: Someone states that ale is their main drink.
explanation.walkthrough: I here is an island, though not a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme makes I mean an island, and this Mediterranean nation is one.

clue.text: Wet behind the ears, water running back

indicators.note: running back means flowing in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: Water runs back behind someone's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' looks literal, prompting thoughts of water, but the whole phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone inexperienced or innocent, unworldly and green.

clue.text: Ultimately dependable teammate behind winger always

indicators.note: behind means following after, so the teammate comes after the winger
ultimately means finally, so the last letter of dependable is taken

parts.note: a tern is a bird, a creature with wings
an ally is someone on your side

explanation.surface: A footballer's reliable teammate is always backing up the winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a football position, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means forever, for all time, without end.

clue.text: True as religious teachings

parts.note: as in the sense of because means since
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A claim that something is true, as religious doctrine says.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and heartfelt feelings are true ones, without pretence.

clue.text: Musical location of many I's, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: the country with many of this puzzle's islands is Greece

explanation.surface: A query about a musical set among many islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The country Greece, spoken, matches the title of the 1971 musical later filmed with John Travolta.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous stage show and film about 1950s American high school life.
